one_liner: Tiny no_std message-loop runtime for Rust/Wasm apps; its hand-written DOM benchmark matches vanilla JS, not faster.
what_it_does: DeLorean is about 200 lines of no_std Rust: an App trait with hidden __hydrate, __dispatch and __render hooks, a run! macro that leaks the app into a static Addr, and a Copy handle (DeLorean<App>) whose send(msg) queues a message. It drains the whole queue through __dispatch, then calls __render once. It has no templates, virtual DOM, diffing or components. You write the DOM code yourself with web-sys; the trait docs say the hooks are meant to be generated by a derive, but the crate (split out of yarte in October 2020) ships none. It is not a drop-in for React or any JS framework.
how_it_is_fast: The speed in the suite comes from the benchmark's hand-written web-sys code, not from the crate. That code clones a prebuilt <tr> template with cloneNode(true) and keeps direct references to each row's id, label and delete nodes. It updates only text marked dirty in per-row and app-level u8 bitmasks, and reuses rows non-keyed: swap rewrites two rows' text, and replace-all rewrites text in place. Delete removes the row node directly. The crate itself adds only message batching (all queued messages are dispatched, then one render) through a leaked static with no reference counting or RefCell.
when_to_use: Small Rust/Wasm widgets where you would write direct web-sys DOM updates anyway and want a minimal single-threaded message-loop skeleton (dispatch, then one render) with no framework runtime.
Non-keyed tables and lists whose rows can be rewritten in place: the suite build ran swap rows in 8.2 ms and replace-all in 12.7 ms on an Apple M4 in Chrome 154.

Studying how fast plain web-sys DOM code can get from Rust: in the same suite data it is level with vanillajs-non-keyed (1.010x the time) and ranks 7th of 67 non-keyed entries, the fastest Rust entry.
no_std Wasm builds that only need alloc.
when_not_to_use: Speed over plain JavaScript: across the nine CPU benchmarks it takes 1.010x vanillajs-non-keyed's time and 1.112x vanillajs-3-non-keyed's (derived from page data), so the README's 'Fastest than vanillajs' is not supported.
Apps that need templates, components, keyed lists, SSR or reactivity: the crate provides none, and the measured speed belongs to the hand-written DOM code you would have to write yourself.

Bundle-size-sensitive pages: the suite build ships 36.1 kB compressed (101.1 kB uncompressed) against Kobold's 9.7 kB and Svelte 5's 6.7 kB (suite units, presumably kB); ready memory is 1.75 MB vs React's 1.19 MB.
Anything that needs maintenance or a community: last commit 2023-03-30, 4 stars, 23 commits, about 6k all-time crates.io downloads and 19 recent ones.
Non-Wasm targets or multi-threaded use: lib.rs has compile_error!("only compile in wasm32") for every other target, and the runtime is single-threaded by design.

integration.dependencies: none at runtime (no_std plus alloc); build-dependency yarte_helpers ~0.15.8 (toolchain detection). The benchmark app adds wasm-bindgen, web-sys, js-sys, serde, serde_json and rand 0.7.
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.65 per the README (edition 2021; no rust-version field in Cargo.toml); built with wasm-pack for wasm32-unknown-unknown
integration.platforms: wasm32 only (compile_error! on other targets since 'fix: remove native implementations', 2023-03-30); browser via wasm-bindgen
integration.thread_safety: Single-threaded only. The context holds Cell and UnsafeCell, so the handle cannot be shared across threads; on nightly it is also marked !Send and !Sync explicitly. Re-entrancy is guarded by a ready flag, and send() during a dispatch only queues the message.

gotchas: Benchmark-code bug (does not affect the measured numbers): run_n, behind Create 1,000 and Create 10,000, overwrites existing rows and only appends, never truncating. Clicking Create 1,000 after Create 10,000 therefore leaves 10,000 rows, with only the first 1,000 replaced. The suite's measured sequences (create from empty, replace 1,000 with 1,000, create 10,000 from empty) never shrink the table, so the timings stand. Also, clicking an already selected row deselects it (a toggle the other implementations do not have). The same code is in the repo at examples/js-framework-benchmark (handler.rs and app.rs identical to the suite copy).

build.rs sets cfg(nightly) whenever a nightly compiler is detected. That turns the queue's unwrap into core::intrinsics::unreachable (undefined behaviour if it is ever None) and needs the unstable core_intrinsics and negative_impls features, so behaviour and buildability change silently with the toolchain.

run! wraps the unsafe A::run, which must be called exactly once. The app is leaked with Box::leak and never freed, and Addr's Drop panics in release builds. The __render, __hydrate and __dispatch hooks are #[doc(hidden)] defaults that do nothing unless you override them.

Version labels are stale: the suite calls the entry v0.1.0, its Cargo.toml pins delorean 0.2.1 (2020-10-06), and the checked-in bundled-dist was built with an unrecorded rustc and wasm-bindgen; the current 0.3.0 (2023-03-30) is unmeasured. The comparison with React is cross-mode (non-keyed vs keyed hooks): swap 8.2 vs 89.7 ms carries most of the 0.522x. The results.ts snapshot is marked unofficial (isOfficial = false).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Against Kobold, the other catalogued non-keyed Rust entry, CPU time is a tie (0.978x Kobold's time, derived from page data), but Kobold ships 9.7 kB compressed against 36.1 kB and offers a real view macro, so Kobold wins. Delorean also adds little over the hand-written wasm-bindgen/web-sys entry (0.893x its time, cross-mode non-keyed vs keyed). Pick Leptos, Sycamore or rust-dominator for an actual framework; consider DeLorean only as a minimal message-loop skeleton for hand-written DOM code.
verified_claims_summary: In krausest/js-framework-benchmark's Chrome 154.0.8037.98 development snapshot (Apple M4 MacBook Pro 14, macOS 26.6.2, isOfficial = false), the delorean-v0.1.0-non-keyed build (delorean 0.2.1, release lto, panic=abort) took 0.522x the time of react-hooks-v19.2.0-keyed. That is the unweighted geometric mean of the nine median total durations, which I reproduced from results.ts, and it compares non-keyed with keyed. Against like-for-like non-keyed vanilla JS it is 1.010x (vanillajs-non-keyed) and 1.112x (vanillajs-3-non-keyed), i.e. not faster; per row, create 1,000 is 22.9 vs 23.6 ms for React and create 10,000 is 237.4 vs 401.0 ms.
status_note: Abandoned since 2023-03-30 (4 stars, crate 0.3.0, 19 recent downloads); MIT or Apache-2.0 and only about 200 lines, so easy to vendor, but it contributes only a message queue and the speed comes from DOM code you write yourself.
